claims.text: Pre-sintering functionalization of ZrB2 powder with an ultrathin HfC coating will enable full densification at approximately 1700 °C.
HfC-coated ZrB2 will have better oxidation resistance than conventionally sintered ZrB2 and previous lower-temperature variants.
HfC-coated ZrB2 will have better liquid plating-metal corrosion durability than conventionally sintered ZrB2 and previous lower-temperature variants.
CVD at around 1200 °C under an inert atmosphere can form a uniform nanometer-scale HfC coating on ZrB2 powder.
The coated powder can be consolidated by SPS at approximately 1700 °C and 50–100 MPa using rapid heating and cooling.
The nanometer-scale HfC layer will become incorporated at powder surfaces and grain boundaries during SPS.
The incorporated HfC layer will reduce interfacial energy.
The incorporated HfC layer will act as a barrier during service.
HfC coating reduces the surface energy of ZrB2 particles.
Reduced surface energy enhances diffusion bonding and facilitates lower-temperature densification.
The incorporated HfC layer inhibits oxygen ingress into the sintered body.
The incorporated HfC layer inhibits penetration by liquid plating metal.
Suppressing oxygen and liquid-metal penetration will mitigate oxidation and corrosion while maintaining mechanical integrity.
HfC-coated ZrB2 densified at approximately 1700 °C will have mechanical properties comparable to or better than ZrB2 conventionally sintered above 2300 °C.
HfC-coated ZrB2 will exhibit significantly lower oxidation rates or thinner oxide scales.
HfC-coated ZrB2 will exhibit reduced susceptibility to liquid-metal corrosion under high-temperature service conditions.
Successful scale-up requires preservation of uniform HfC coating quality.
